goals: Maintain one Fabric mod, source tree, build, version, and deployable JAR for the absorbed Nibaru native material catalog and all BGE geometry.
Preserve every former Nibaru and BGE registry/resource identity, specialized material behavior, and saved-world reference while CNM remains an unchanged external dependency.
Expose one deterministic ordered geometry catalog for Vertical Slab, Step, Corner, Quarter Column, and Layer without changing established placement, economy, or material-frame semantics.

Offer complete nine-role BGE geometry families for the exact 148 explicitly cataloged optional-provider sources when Ribbits, Mynx Trees, Macaw's Paths, Building But Better, Enderscape, or Mossy Stone supplies the corresponding source block, without discovering or completing arbitrary CNM families.

Treat adding a normal catalog material as full membership in the canonical block, horizontal slab, stair, wall, Vertical Slab, Step, Layer, Corner, and Quarter Column roles unless an exact technical exclusion is recorded.
Keep canonical material identity separate from geometry generation so limited special forms such as Farmland Slab remain explicitly canonical-bound without implying a full generated family.
Require every BGE-owned registered block to have one explicit canonical classification or a documented exemption, with bootstrap validation preventing anonymous material-semantic holes.

Expose each valid binding's rendered surface as deterministic canonical-face patches with exact sixteenth planes, in-plane footprints, and explicitly typed terrain-height relationships for material-agnostic consumers.
scope: Compile the retained `games.twinhead.moreslabsstairsandwalls` source and `more_slabs_stairs_and_walls` resources directly inside BGE with a clear LGPL-covered source and attribution boundary.
Register native slabs, stairs, walls, material profiles, transitions, and client bindings before deriving CNM/BGE geometry through one guarded bootstrap and one root Fabric descriptor.

Preserve all native material profiles, canonical parents, copied settings, TOP/SIDE/BOTTOM roles, axes, patterns, tint, translucency, transitions, drops, and specialized behaviors; C62 corrects the wall-material, canonical-role duplication, leaf-wall, and plain-Path seams demonstrated by exact C61 runtime evidence, C63 corrects external axis-family inventory previews, C64 adds the complete BBB beam catalog, C65 corrects its demonstrated BBB production axis-resource classification failure, C66 gives compatible Quarter Columns Step-equivalent full-cell continuation targeting without changing their physical geometry, C68 preserves one-to-one texel density for axis-material Layer faces without changing their geometry or grain orientation, C69 restores independent material axes to the canonical BBB Beam Slab and Beam Stair, C70 restores vanilla Stone slab ownership, C71 mirrors Minecraft 26.2 horizontal-slab tilling and Farmland lifecycle semantics, C72 extends that Farmland Slab water search exactly one block lower without changing the C71 lifecycle, C73 establishes authoritative typed canonical bindings plus placement-time canonicalization for completed ordinary horizontal and Vertical Slabs, C74 adds Ribbits huge-toadstool material surfaces, C75 adds the generic binding-owned surface-patch contract, C76 makes every visible generated Ribbits toadstool surface use its assigned source-block texture, C77 canonicalizes a newly completed four-Layer blockspace while retaining legacy four-Layer states, C78 completes the contract for every resolved Stair and Wall state with authoritative union-tiled surfaces, and C79 adds three current Minecraft parent families plus a generic, resource-contract-verified CNM axis-pillar bridge.

C92 restores C78's explicit material/profile architecture and removes C79-C91 arbitrary-CNM discovery. C93 and C94 preserve the explicit provider catalog, role ownership, placed resources, and item presentation. C99 removes the C95-C98 spruce tint interception and tracing experiment, restores the exact C94 spruce/client contract, and retains C96's generated Veiled Leaves and Silver Birch Leaves Stair frames. C99 also makes Bookshelf Corner, Quarter Column, and Layer top/bottom faces select the existing Matcha bookshelf-top resource only while the active pack supplies it, keeps valid oak-planks fallback and Bookshelf side faces, and locks Bookshelf Stair wood UVs to the Minecraft 26.2 non-directional Stair frame without changing physical shape or placement.

Generate one Layer, Corner, and Quarter Column per supported canonical family while preserving Vertical Slab and Step, deterministic selector order, one-source economy, orientation, waterlogging, collision, and drops.

Provide primary Fabric ID `cnm_terrain_slabs_compat` and verified legacy alias `more_slabs_stairs_and_walls` from the same mod container and shared version `4.2.44-bge.canary100.bbb-beam-compat-visibility+26.2`.

Preserve C58 native registry/resource identities while exposing one canonical nine-role family per exact optional source variant: 52 Macaw patterned full blocks plus five distinct Macaw soil Path blocks, six Mynx Trees log/wood/leaf sources, Ribbits Mossy Oak Planks plus Red Toadstool, Brown Toadstool, and Toadstool Stem, all 12 BBB beam parents including Pale Oak, 68 exact Enderscape sources, and the provider-owned Mossy Stone root. C93 adopts exact vanilla or Enderscape Slab/Stairs/Wall blocks wherever supplied, suppresses overlapping fallback registrations while Enderscape is loaded, supplies only genuinely absent standard roles plus the five BGE-specific roles, and validates exactly one visible nine-role ShapeMap variation for each explicit family. The six stripped Enderscape log/wood/stem/hyphae entries retain their exact canonical side/end contracts without fabricated stripping transitions. Enderscape's actual `nebulite_block` is the requested Block of Nebulite and `raw_shadoline_block` is the requested Block of Raw Shadoline; absent `block_of_raw_magnia` remains a declared exclusion. The three Ribbits toadstools remain distinct source identities; every exposed face of each generated BGE role uses that source's assigned exterior texture, with no generated `toadstool_inside` route and no provider texture bytes included. BBB's original slab and stair registrations remain untouched but are excluded from canonical selectors; C69's BGE AxisSlab and AxisStairs remain canonical, BBB's thin Beam Wall topology remains canonical for all 12 Beam families, and the three Enderscape private Beam variants preserve that topology with their own palettes.

exclusions: C89 changes only CNM/BGE family-root classification after normal first-pass family completion: every canonically bound non-root role, whether supplied as a normal slab, stair, wall, Vertical Slab, Step, Layer, Corner, or Quarter Column, is rejected as a later CNM source by both Slab and Stair scan branches. It adds no name- or provider-specific exclusion, synthetic geometry combination, canonical binding, validation bypass, registration, resource, placement, economy, CTM, or provider-behavior change.

C90 changes only the C87 deferred-CNM-Wall lifecycle after ShapeMap resolves a component: when that resolved component already has a real provider Wall, BGE retires and explicitly exempts its preregistered provisional deferred Wall rather than injecting or binding it; when the component has no real Wall, the same provisional block remains its normal canonical Wall. This is component- and role-based, not a material, namespace, provider, or Enderscape compatibility path; it creates no synthetic binding, does not weaken validation, does not alter C89's non-root guard, and does not change normal CNM family autopopulation, registration, geometry, placement, economy, CTM, resources, or provider behavior.

C92 makes the C79-C91 arbitrary-CNM/deferred completion path historical only: unknown CNM materials remain CNM-owned and receive no BGE registrations, inferred identities, or selector rewrites; only explicit profile definitions may contribute BGE families.

C93 changes only explicitly cataloged provider-family ownership and the shared rendering contracts requested for Walls, item/selector previews, lowered Path culling and Step UVs, and Corrupt Overgrowth state projection. Item-only preview transforms do not alter placed blockstates or world model rotations; no arbitrary discovery, generic root inference, deferred/profile-free family, provisional block, `*_slab_wall`, or post-resolution material guessing returns.

C94 changes only item/selector presentation: it removes the C93-only catalog display override, restores each affected item's C92 model chain, and routes all 15 Beam Vertical Slab and Step items through inventory-only wrappers over their unchanged direct-Y placed models. It changes no placed blockstate or block-model resource, texture artwork, registration, placement rule, geometry state, provider ownership, selector order, economy, or architecture boundary.

C99 selectively removes only the abandoned C95-C98 spruce tint/trace path and the exact Sodium diagnostic dependency. It retains C94 spruce/client behavior and C96's two-family tinted-Stair model-frame correction. Its Bookshelf changes use the existing resource-pack-controlled `minecraft:block/bookshelf_top` seam when supplied, with oak-planks fallback and unchanged Bookshelf sides; only the native Bookshelf Stair blockstate UV-lock selectors change among packaged placed resources. Native `minecraft:spruce_leaves` assets, visible tint ownership, all placement/collision/item behavior, other catalog families, and external Foundation resources remain outside BGE.

C100 changes only the CNM shared creative/search presentation predicate for the exact 24 retained BBB Beam Slab/Stair compatibility identities. Those registered BBB items remain outside ShapeMap and all canonical BGE roles; BGE axis-aware Beam Slab/Stairs, BBB Beam Walls, selector membership/order, private Murublight/Celestial/Veiled Beam families, registrations, recipes, placement, rendering, geometry, textures, and persistence identities are unchanged.
Clutter No More source and artifacts remain external and unchanged; its ShapeMap remains the canonical family and switching mechanism.
C58 is limited to the user-authored glass-Corner geometry/UV route; generic glass Quarter Column projection and all non-glass Corner outputs remain C57-equivalent.

C68 changes only normal axis-material Layer face UV rectangles: it preserves Layer bounds, placement, collision, state, texture roles, grain rotation, special visual paths, non-axis materials, all other geometries, registration, data, display transforms, and external-material support.
`projects/bge-ctm`, shaders, resource-pack classification, BBB source/assets, and unrelated consumer projects are outside this consolidation.
Accepted BGE C52 and historical standalone Nibaru C45 are preserved as rollback provenance and are not rewritten.

C72 owns only the C71 Farmland Slab hydration search extension from Y..Y+1 to Y-1..Y+1; hoe conversion, moisture range/progression, rain, drying, crop retention, survival, trampling, Dirt-slab reversion, geometry, drops, waterlogging, Dirt Path, non-farmland geometry, and C70 Stone behavior remain unchanged. Crop placement, crop growth, partial-height projection, targeting, particles, and rendering remain deferred to Slab Decorations.

C73 changes canonical material classification, state projection, and the already-legal BlockItem placement result only for completed normal-catalog horizontal and Vertical Slabs. It adds no recipe, refund, migration, or broader occupancy normalization; historical double states remain valid, and special Farmland Slab is explicitly excluded from canonical full-block replacement.

C75 introduced the BGE-owned surface contract; C78 now supplies authoritative resolved-state surfaces for every ordinary Stair and Wall configuration. The contract still does not decide CTM rules, connect materials, or render overlays.

C76 changes only generated Ribbits Red Toadstool, Brown Toadstool, and Toadstool Stem texture selection plus the human-facing BGE Canary filename. Provider-owned source-block rendering, every non-toadstool family, geometry, economy, behavior, canonical identity, and the C75 surface-semantics API remain unchanged.

C77 changes only successful placement of the fourth matching normal-catalog Layer and the legacy four-Layer fallback model for uniform-textured HugeMushroomBlock providers. Layers one through three, failed or incompatible placement, legacy four-Layer state validity, recipes, drops, family identities, C75 surface semantics, C76 generated toadstool texture semantics, and provider-owned canonical source-block rendering remain unchanged.

C78 changes only binding-owned surface descriptions for resolved Stair and Wall state plus their validation. It adds no CTM or rendering policy, changes no block registration, state, collision, placement, economy, resource model, material identity, or consumer-specific rule, and leaves `projects/bge-ctm` untouched.

C79 adds normal BGE families for `minecraft:chiseled_resin_bricks`, `minecraft:chiseled_cinnabar`, and axis-aware `minecraft:purpur_pillar`; regular walls remain ordinary no-AXIS WallBlocks. C80 removes C79's registry-wide external axis scanner and uses stock CNM as an external dependency. C81 separates preregistration from family identity: it records real CNM admissions, preregisters inert BGE tail candidates without inventing a parent, then uses CNM's actual resolved ShapeMap component to bind or discard them and completes every known BGE profile in that same component. C82 closes the remaining profile-free resolved branch with canonical-source drops and generated normal client geometry read only after ShapeMap resolution; catalog-only role tags remain typed-profile indexes. C83 writes every BGE-owned generated client resource to both CNM's in-memory resource view and its namespace-preserving client runtime pack path, and adds only the exact Enderscape catalog after the provider's own initialization; it does not copy Enderscape assets, modify CNM, manufacture `block_of_raw_magnia`, alter existing provider ownership, placement, economy, CTM, or unverified runtime behavior. C84 corrects the Blistered Magnia `ofFullCopy` state-callback seam through an explicit Enderscape material-state bridge: geometry state remains separate while Nebulite power, Magnia power, Blistered Magnia polarity, and Blinklamp luminance are carried into every derived role. C85 changes only generated-item tint inheritance: a present canonical item tint array is copied, while a valid model-only canonical item definition keeps its generated block-model/source-provider tint path and does not throw. C86 classifies the exact shared global `facing` property only when an Enderscape DirectionalBlock-derived Layer completes to its canonical source. C87 keeps registry admission separate from every fresh stock-CNM ShapeMap construction: resolved BGE roles are re-injected idempotently into each new graph, a deferred ordinary Wall contributes only when that graph has none, and first-bake resource output uses an admitted visual source without electing a canonical parent. C87 also corrects the exact Enderscape visual contracts for stripped axial sources, terrain/path structural UV mappings, Void Shale, Blinklamp, and model-owned foliage tint fallback. C88 changes only resource-variable resolution when an already admitted CNM visual source has no direct `models/block/<block-id>.json`: it follows that source's provider blockstate model references and resolves an existing ordinary texture contract. It does not change CNM admission or ShapeMap resolution, invent a canonical parent, change BBB/CNM, copy provider textures, omit valid BBB beam families, or alter registry identities, geometry, placement, economy, CTM, or provider-only behavior. C91 adds the three Enderscape Beam roots through private local assembly from the exact locally supplied BBB artwork and Enderscape palettes. BBB source bytes, derivative texture bytes, and the resulting JAR are PRIVATE_LOCAL_ONLY: no such bytes may be tracked, distributed, released, uploaded, or placed in public resource paths; build output and ignored local artifact retention are the sole authorized storage. The exact Enderscape audit records source behavior boundaries rather than claiming that non-projected provider interactions are inherited.
